title: Zoom Video Conferencing: Complete Architecture
description: Design zoom video conferencing with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a video conferencing platform similar to Zoom that supports multi-party video calls, screen sharing, in-meeting chat, cloud recording, breakout rooms, and waiting rooms. The system must manage real-time media routing through Selective Forwarding Units (SFUs), handle signaling for WebRTC negotiation, and scale to thousands of concurrent meetings with adaptive bitrate based on network conditions.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Schedule meetings with calendar integration, recurring options, and passcode protection
Join meetings via desktop client, web client, mobile app, or dial-in phone number
Host controls: mute participants, remove attendees, enable waiting room, and lock meeting
Breakout rooms: split main meeting into sub-rooms with host broadcast and timer
Screen sharing with remote control, annotation tools, and multi-share support
In-meeting chat with direct messages, group chat, and file sharing
Cloud recording with speaker view, gallery view, and separate audio/video tracks
Live transcription and closed captions in multiple languages
Virtual backgrounds, blur, and touch-up appearance using client-side ML models
Post-meeting analytics: attendance duration, participant list, chat logs, and recording playback

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Meeting join time under 5 seconds from clicking link to first video frame
Sub-150ms latency for audio packets with jitter buffer to mask network variation
99.99% availability for meeting infrastructure with automatic failover across regions
Support 1,000 participants per meeting with SFU cascading for large rooms
Recording is stored within 2 minutes of meeting end with redundant object storage
End-to-end encryption option for enterprise meetings with client-side key exchange

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application that validates the Zoom conferencing domain: meeting scheduling, signaling state machine, chat messages, recording metadata, and participant management. This validates WebRTC negotiation flows before splitting media handling into separate services.

data.title: Monolith Tech Stack
data.code:
Frontend:
  - React 18 with TypeScript
  - Vite for build tooling
  - Tailwind CSS for styling
  - React Query for server state

Backend (ASP.NET Core):
  - Minimal API or MVC Controllers
  - Entity Framework Core for data access
  - Azure SQL Database or AWS RDS for relational data
  - Built-in DI, logging, and health checks

Infrastructure:
  - Azure App Service or AWS EC2/ECS
  - Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for file assets
  - Azure Monitor or AWS CloudWatch for logging
  - Single database with tables for all domains

data.text: As traffic grows, split the monolith into independently scalable microservices. Each service owns its data and communicates via async messaging or REST/gRPC.

items: Signaling Service: Manages WebRTC signaling state machine including SDP offer/answer exchange, ICE candidate trickling, and SFU transport negotiation. Uses WebSocket connections with heartbeat and automatic reconnection for network resilience.

SFU Media Service: Operates Selective Forwarding Units that receive upstream video/audio tracks and forward selected subsets to each participant. Implements simulcast and SVC to serve different quality layers based on subscriber bandwidth and viewport size.

Recording Service: Orchestrates cloud recording by subscribing to SFU media streams, mixing audio and video tracks, and storing packaged recordings in object storage. Supports separate tracks for post-production editing and transcription jobs.
Chat Service: Handles in-meeting text chat, direct messages, file attachments, and message reactions. Delivers chat with low latency using a dedicated WebSocket channel separate from signaling.

Meeting Scheduler Service: Manages meeting lifecycle from creation through completion, enforces passcodes and waiting rooms, assigns media servers by region, and publishes meeting metadata to calendar integrations.

Screen Share Service: Handles screen and application capture from presenter clients, optimizes video encoding with hardware acceleration, and provides remote control streams with input event relay for controlled sessions.

data.title: React App Structure
data.code:
src/
  features/
    ZoomConferencingHld/
      components/
        VideoGallery/        # Adaptive grid with spotlight, filmstrip, and speaker view
        AudioVisualizer/     # Speaking indicator with waveform and mute/deafen badges
        ScreenShareView/     # Remote screen canvas with annotation toolbar
        ChatPanel/           # Collapsible chat with mentions, file upload, search
        WaitingRoom/         # Host view of lobby with admit/deny controls
        BreakoutRooms/       # Host controls for creating, broadcasting, and closing rooms
        RecordingControls/   # Start/stop/pause recording with consent banner
        VirtualBackground/   # Background selection with blur slider and image picker
      hooks/
        useWebRTC/           # Peer connection management with adaptive bitrate
        useSignaling/        # WebSocket signaling with exponential backoff reconnect
        useMediaDevices/     # Camera/mic enumeration, device selection, permission handling
      api/
        meetings.ts          # POST /meetings, GET /meetings/:id, PATCH /meetings/:id/status
        chat.ts              # GET /meetings/:id/chat, POST /meetings/:id/chat/messages
        recording.ts         # POST /meetings/:id/recordings, GET /meetings/:id/recordings
      store/
        meetingStore.ts      # Meeting ID, participant list, host controls, breakout state
        mediaStore.ts        # Local tracks, remote streams, mute state, device prefs

Key Patterns:
  - Feature-based folder structure
  - API Gateway as single entry point
  - React Query for metadata caching with aggressive refetch on meeting join
  - WebRTC API directly for peer connections with adaptive bitrate via BWE
  - Canvas for virtual background segmentation with TensorFlow.js WASM backend
